_about: 3-10, re-flown on wave 4a's build (WAKE, step 163: a sleeper whose support is destroyed wakes before the step that would leave it
hanging, as Box2D's DestroyBody does, b2Contact.cpp:101-109). The last route (wave 3b-2) waited about 600 ticks for knight B to
fall; it now falls the tick its wall breaks, and the stone that breaks the wall came down on it in every variant tried (crush on
512 to 519), so that route's idea - the knight carries the key through a portal pair to the keyhole - was not flown again (keeping
the knight alive was not tried). This route is a different solution, with TWO portals: the player takes the key himself, from
the knight the stone crushes.
The walk is the old one's: left off the start platform from tick 28 to 196, down the ramp onto lift_ent_1318 (the player stands on it
at x 107.9; he must be on it between about x 89 and 122, the lift being 64 to 128 wide) and a touch on it (200, "shot": false) sends it
up (lift_sent 201). The lift is at its top from 366, the player's centre at y 126.4 from 367. From the top a shot at (340, 30), over the
right half of breakable_wall_1316, clears single_block_plat_1275 (tap 358, fired on 359 as the lift settles; 342 to 376 win; it flies 73 ticks and
the portal opens on 432), and a shot at (65, 96), beside rolling_stone_1198 (tap 448, fired on 449; 431 to 462 and 466 to 488 win,
463 to 465 are the lift tap's own ticks, one pointer), opens the second on 458 and the stone goes through at once (traversal 458). The
stone comes out at (340, 30), falls on the wall's right half and breaks it on 479 (hit 4.3). Knight B (minion_spawn_913) has stood
since tick ~290 on the wall's left end at (276.6, 128.4), holding its 15 s at wayB1 with key_ent_1271 (it took it on 78): WAKE
wakes it on 479 when its wall goes and it falls (landed on ramp_left 511); the stone, coming down the same way from the wall,
crushes it on 515 (hit 18.9 against 1.23, G1b), and the key, which a knight carries at its chest, is let go of by its dead owner
(Keys.cpp, Carry::Drop) and lies where he stood, at (277.8, 313.5), on the ramp, in reach of anyone who walks by.
The lift is sent down on 465 (tap 464; 424 to 446 and 450 to 504 win), the player stands at its foot from ~626. He walks right
from 618 (588 to 626 win; off the lift a few units above its foot) down the ramp, takes the key on 673 at x ~253 (a character within
26 of it takes it, keys.json) and stops at x 272 on 680, short of the stone resting against the door (a touch of it reads 1.44
and is harmless, but this stays clear), then walks back left up the ramp and over the lift to the keyhole (683 to 820; 673 to 713 and
790 to 850 win), the key trailing him and opening keyhole_ent_1196 when it is within 26 of it (unlocked 790; the key flies in on
832; keyhole and door_locked_ent_1195 gone on 882, which wakes the stone: it rolls right to the wall at x 482 by ~970). He waits at the
wall (x 8) and walks right from 850 (820 to 863 win with a win_by of 1030; the start sets the win, won = start + 167), down the
ramp, behind the stone and past its place, into the door: won on tick 1017.
Leans on: WAKE (the knight falls), G1b's stone crush (the knight dies at the ramp and the key is free), G2's waiting lift, the key's
pickup by the player, R23's tap rules (the wall shot's head-height retry fires on 359 with a drift of 0.96 px). No knight sights or
shoots him (the run has no spot or shot line). Unlocks no achievement: the door line reads medal 2 (silver:
2 portals are within the golden score, but one crystal of three is taken, the two at x 272, y 150 and 182 being out of his walk)
and 16.3 s, and 56 asks gold within 15 s. Not measured on the original: that the knight lands where the stone then crushes it, and
that the key stays free for the player to take. If the original's knight walks out of the stone's way (it lands only 4 ticks before the
crush; here a knight lifted off its floor never walks again under G1a's blocked-way rule, R3c-4), the designed solution is the knight

carrying the key and this route is a workaround for a port gap (a row for the final comparison). Margins, from a scan that moved every tap and walk edge by up to 40 ticks and each aim point by 12 units: the aim
points pass at 12 either way, the taps have 14 ticks or more, the walks 8 or more, and the least are 6, on the first walk's start
(28 within 20 to 34) and end (196 within 190 to 204), which set where he stands on the lift.
